A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PODS research work. Their complete main texts, equations, proofs, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and corresponding experiments can be matched despite reordering.

before.justification: v3 reports original training, accuracy, runtime, down-sampling ablation and completion-length results on GSM8K and MATH.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds chemistry experiments, normalization comparisons and evaluations on additional test sets.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 adds percentile down-sampling as an alternative PODS rule, selecting evenly spaced reward quantiles. The principal max-variance procedure, Algorithms 1–2 and normalization using selected rollouts remain unchanged; normalization before selection is evaluated only as an ablation.

E1.justification: v4 expands beyond mathematical reasoning by training and evaluating on SciKnowEval's L3 Chemistry subset, with multiple-choice answers. Appendix A.5 also evaluates GSM8K-trained Qwen and Llama models on GSM8K Platinum and MATH, adding contamination-focused and cross-benchmark testing scenarios.

E2.justification: The down-sampling comparison expands from max-variance, max-reward and random selection to include percentile selection. Appendix A.3 additionally evaluates full-batch normalization against selected-batch normalization. The main GRPO and GRPO-GA comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v4 adds a normalization control and evaluation of trained checkpoints on additional test sets; chemistry uses direct answer-letter correctness checking. After matching reordered settings, Table 2 reports vanilla GRPO batch sizes changing from 16 to 8 for Llama/GSM8K and from 8 to 16 for Qwen/MATH. These entries contradict Section 4.1's matched-update-size description and do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.3 tests whether advantage normalization should use the full or selected rollout batch. New Appendix A.5 tests generalization beyond the original test set using GSM8K Platinum and MATH. The retained selection-rule ablation also gains percentile selection, substantially extending the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions describe shaded uncertainty bands as 1.96 times the standard error of the mean. The added plots follow this convention, and neither version specifies run counts, seeds or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v4 adds chemistry results, including a 1.8× speedup in Table 3, percentile-selection results, normalization results and four additional-test curves. The five matched original speedup ratios remain unchanged. Some existing timing values change: Figure 4's n=64, m=16 runtime rises from approximately 10.1 to 11.6 seconds per step. Figure 5's selection-rule runtime results are removed.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 newly specifies the percentile rule mathematically through reward quantiles 0.5/m, 1.5/m, through (m−0.5)/m. The formal PODS definition, variance objective, Lemma 3.1, Theorems 1–2 and their proofs remain unchanged; no additional theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: v4 removes the conclusion's algorithm-agnostic characterization and explicitly restricts empirical and theoretical claims to PODS within GRPO. Its stated demonstrated applicability expands from mathematics to mathematics and chemistry. The central efficiency claim, minimum 1.7× speedup claim and efficient max-variance contribution are retained.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive discussion of why selected-batch normalization may help and interprets additional-test results as evidence against test-set-specific overfitting. Section 5 explicitly qualifies transfer to other RL algorithms and discusses potential prompt imbalance under pooled selection, motivating prompt balancing and alternative selection criteria. These extend the earlier limitations and mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: v4 documents chemistry reward checking and its hyperparameters, and adds a reproducibility statement describing anonymized supplementary code and public datasets/models. The experimental GitHub link already appears in v3. The new statement promises a future public code release despite retaining that link, introducing ambiguity rather than establishing new availability.

R1.justification: v4 adds Feng et al.'s SciKnowEval reference and Zheng et al.'s GRESO work to the prompt-selection discussion. GRESO is cited but not experimentally compared. The broader related-work narrative and claimed distinction between within-prompt rollout selection and prompt filtering remain stable.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized wording and explanatory edits, moves the selection-rule comparison from Appendix A.3 to Section 4.3, and reorganizes the appendix around the added analyses. Section 5 gains scope and reproducibility paragraphs, while the overall introduction–related work–method–experiments–conclusion structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a different publication template, author layout, typography and page geometry. Figure 3 expands and reorders experiment panels; Figure 5 moves into the main text and replaces runtime bars with a zoomed accuracy panel. New normalization and generalization figures are added, tables gain chemistry entries, and completion-length figures are reordered and expanded.

improvement.justification: The chemistry evaluation, additional-test checks and normalization ablation strengthen evidence for applicability and design choices, while the explicit GRPO scope better aligns claims with demonstrated support. However, v4 introduces conflicting baseline batch sizes in Table 2 and inconsistent code-release wording. These reporting problems limit the overall gain despite the useful additional evidence.
